featured.title: Nadella, Pichai, and Arora Just Bought a Cricket Team at Lord's. They Paid £145 Million.
featured.excerpt: A consortium of eleven Silicon Valley executives, most of Indian origin, outbid Sanjiv Goenka to take a 49 per cent stake in London Spirit — the most expensive franchise deal in The Hundred's history.
featured.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, who led the Silicon Valley consortium's bid for London Spirit
featured.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech CEOs who run America's biggest companies are now buying up global cricket franchises, with Indian or Indian-origin investors holding stakes in five of eight Hundred teams — a cultural and financial statement for the diaspora.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Gulf Ceasefire Unravels as Iran Fires Missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain. India’s Seafarers Pay the Price.
news.excerpt: Three Indian sailors are dead, 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, and the fragile US-Iran deal is falling apart — leaving New Delhi caught between its closest strategic partner and its citizens’ safety.
news.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman that has become the epicenter of the US-Iran conflict.
news.image_credit: NASA/MODIS, Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
news.nri_angle: India's 9 million Gulf workers face direct risk from the escalation. Three Indian seafarers died on the MT Settebello, prompting India to summon the US envoy. Thousands more remain stranded on ships in the Gulf. India's oil imports and domestic inflation are directly tied to Hormuz stability.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Amazon Just Raised Its India Bet to $48 Billion. The Quick Commerce War It Triggered Is Already Drawing Blood.
news.excerpt: Andy Jassy's visit to New Delhi came with $13 billion in fresh AI and cloud commitments — and a 300-city quick commerce expansion that has wiped $15 billion off Blinkit and Swiggy's market value.
news.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy meets Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to discuss the company's expanded India investment
news.nri_angle: NRIs invested in Indian quick commerce stocks face margin compression, while the $80B+ hyperscaler buildout creates high-paying AI jobs and transforms the Indian startup ecosystem
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America's New Ambassador to India Says the Visa Crackdown Isn't About India. Here's What He's Not Saying.
news.excerpt: Sergio Gor insists H-1B reforms are part of a 'broader overhaul,' not targeted at Indians. But a new wage-based selection system could shut out the entry-level workers who built Silicon Valley's outsourcing pipeline.
news.image_caption: U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor at the White House
news.nri_angle: Indians are 72% of H-1B recipients and dominate the green card backlog — the shift to wage-based selection could reshape the pathway that brought millions of Indian professionals to America
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Hyderabad Names Road 'Donald Trump Avenue' in First Such Honour for a US President in India
news.excerpt: Telangana's Congress government renamed a road near the US Consulate and tech offices of Microsoft, Google, and Amazon as part of a broader initiative to position Hyderabad as a global innovation hub — drawing both praise from Trump and sharp political backlash at home.
news.image_caption: US President Donald Trump thanked India for the road naming honour in Hyderabad, calling it a historic first for a US president.
news.image_credit: White House official portrait, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
news.nri_angle: Hyderabad's Financial District hosts the India offices of Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and many other American tech firms, making it a key nexus for the Indian-American tech workforce. The road naming amid ongoing trade negotiations signals deepening US-India economic ties that directly affect NRI professionals and investors.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Launches Aarogya Setu 2.0, Unveils Sweeping Digital Health Overhaul
news.excerpt: Health Minister JP Nadda rolled out nearly a dozen interconnected platforms — from AI-powered health records and wearable integration to a WhatsApp chatbot and a unified drug registry — in India's most ambitious push yet to digitise healthcare for 1.4 billion people.
news.image_caption: Union Health Minister JP Nadda launched Aarogya Setu 2.0 and a suite of digital health initiatives on June 29, 2026.
news.nri_angle: The ABHA system lets NRIs access family health records remotely, wearable integration connects parents' fitness trackers to a centralised record, the UHI enables cross-border telemedicine, and Scan & Register/Pay simplifies hospital visits for diaspora members visiting India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Pakistan Just Bombed Afghanistan for the Second Time This Month. India Told Islamabad to Stop Blaming Everyone Else.
news.excerpt: After a Karachi Rangers attack killed three soldiers, Pakistan struck militant hideouts across three Afghan provinces. Kabul says the bombs hit civilians. India called Pakistan’s attempt to link it to the Karachi assault ‘baseless.’
news.image_caption: Sindh Rangers paramilitary personnel in Pakistan
news.nri_angle: Nine million Indians work in Gulf states near the conflict zone; a Pakistan-Afghanistan escalation could disrupt migration corridors, energy supply, and regional counterterrorism cooperation that protects diaspora communities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Ever Takes Effect in 16 Days. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora.
news.excerpt: The India-UK Free Trade Agreement launches July 15 with steep tariff cuts, extended pension portability for professionals, and a steel dispute that almost sank it.
news.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at the India-UK FTA signing ceremony
news.nri_angle: The FTA includes extended pension portability for professionals moving between India and the UK, directly affecting 1.6 million people of Indian origin in Britain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Reopened All Three Himalayan Trade Routes With China. The Last Caravan Crossed Seven Years Ago.
news.excerpt: Lipulekh, Shipki La, and Nathu La are all active again for the first time since the Galwan clash. Traders no longer need mules. The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra is back. And for the first time ever, transactions will be in rupees and yuan, not barter.
news.image_caption: The road to Nathu La Pass in Sikkim, one of three Himalayan trade corridors reopened on the India-China border
news.nri_angle: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra’s return restores access to one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for millions of Hindus, Jains, and Buddhists in the diaspora, while the trade reopening signals an India-China normalisation that could reshape investment and travel calculus for NRIs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Kotak Mahindra's CEO Is Leaving After Less Than Three Years. The Bank Has Now Lost Two Leaders Since Its Founder Stepped Down.
news.excerpt: Ashok Vaswani, a Barclays and Citigroup veteran who was handpicked to succeed billionaire Uday Kotak, told the board he will not seek reappointment. The stock fell 3.3 percent.
news.image_caption: Kotak Mahindra Bank, India's fourth-largest private sector lender
news.nri_angle: Kotak Mahindra Bank serves millions of NRI customers through NRE/NRO accounts, remittances, and digital banking — a leadership vacuum at the top affects the diaspora's banking experience directly.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian-Born Billionaire in Canada Just Parked $1 Billion in Indian Bonds. It's Not About the Bonds.
news.excerpt: Prem Watsa's Fairfax bought nearly $1 billion in Indian government debt in a single week — positioning to acquire a majority stake in state-owned IDBI Bank in what could be India's biggest bank privatisation ever.
news.image_caption: Prem Watsa, the Indian-Canadian billionaire who chairs Fairfax Financial Holdings
news.nri_angle: If Prem Watsa's Fairfax wins IDBI Bank, it would be the first time a foreign-origin investor takes control of a major Indian bank — reshaping NRI banking, remittances, and India's privatisation programme.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: They Donated From Abroad to Build the Ram Temple. Eight Men Were Stealing the Money.
news.excerpt: A court in Ayodhya has detained eight men — including banking staff — over the systematic embezzlement of devotee donations at India's most politically charged temple. The racket ran for years.
news.image_caption: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
news.nri_angle: NRIs across the US, UK, Canada, and Gulf donated heavily to the Ram Mandir trust — the embezzlement scandal raises urgent questions about financial governance and accountability for diaspora donors.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Harmanpreet Hit Three Sixes in One Over at Lord's. India's Women Still Went Home.
news.excerpt: India posted their highest-ever T20 World Cup score against Australia — and it wasn't enough. Perry and Gardner's century stand knocked India out at the group stage.
news.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur scored a blistering 56 off 27 balls at Lord's
news.nri_angle: British Indians packed Lord's to cheer the women's team, and NRIs worldwide followed the tournament — India's group-stage exit, coming hours after the men's Ireland debacle, was a painful double blow.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved the Fed From Trump. Here's Why India Should Pay Attention.
news.excerpt: A 5-4 ruling preserving the Federal Reserve's independence has direct implications for the rupee, NRI remittances, and the institutional trust that underpins Indian-American wealth.
news.image_caption: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, whose firing by President Trump was blocked by the Supreme Court
news.nri_angle: Nearly five million Indian-Americans hold US investments and rely on Fed-driven rate decisions — a politicised central bank would introduce sovereign risk to their portfolios and shake the $125 billion remittance corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Central Bank Just Gave NRIs a Reason to Move Their Dollars Home. Banks Are in a Frenzy to Cash In.
news.excerpt: The RBI is bearing the hedging cost on foreign currency deposits so NRIs can earn 7% risk-free on their dollars. Banks are scrambling to attract up to $100 billion, and the diaspora holds the key to rescuing the rupee.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: NRIs can earn 6-7% risk-free on dollar deposits as India's central bank absorbs currency hedging costs — a rare moment when the diaspora's savings are being actively courted to rescue the rupee.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: He Made Ireland Beat India Twice in Three Days. Then He Quit.
news.excerpt: Heinrich Malan is stepping down as Ireland's head coach on the back of cricket's biggest upset of the year. Gary Wilson becomes the first Irish-born coach in over 30 years. India, meanwhile, is in 'disbelief.'
news.nri_angle: India's cricket humiliation in Belfast resonates deeply with the diaspora — many followed the IPL from abroad and now face ribbing from Irish and British colleagues as the team heads to England next.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Launched Two Anti-Dumping Probes in One Week. One Could Make Its Own Power Grid More Expensive.
news.excerpt: New Delhi is cracking down on cheap steel from China, Japan, and Russia — but duties on transformer-grade electrical steel could slow a ₹9 lakh crore grid expansion that India can't afford to delay.
news.nri_angle: India's ₹9 lakh crore power grid expansion — which NRI investors have poured into through infrastructure bonds and mutual funds — could face higher costs if anti-dumping duties raise transformer steel prices, while the trade crackdown on Chinese steel signals shifting investment dynamics in India's manufacturing sector.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Signed a Trade Deal With Europe. Now It's Begging Brussels Not to Cut Off Its Metal Scrap.
news.excerpt: The EU's planned scrap export ban could tighten steel and aluminium supply for India's manufacturers — and undermine a trade agreement that isn't even in force yet.
news.image_caption: Aluminium swarf at a recycling facility in Germany
news.nri_angle: NRIs in European manufacturing, recycling, and commodity trading face direct exposure to the scrap policy shift, while the India-EU trade deal's success — and the investment climate it creates — matters to diaspora professionals and businesses on both sides.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Monsoon Is Running 43% Below Normal. The Last Time It Was This Bad, It Set Off a Food-Price Spiral.
news.excerpt: The Earth Science Ministry says this could be the weakest monsoon in 11 years. Global sugar prices are already surging, Indian markets are wobbling, and 300 districts are on a contingency plan.
news.image_caption: Vraj Acharya, WELL Labs via wikimedia (BY-SA)
news.nri_angle: NRIs with family in farming-dependent states face higher remittance needs if monsoon rains don't recover, while food inflation threatens the cost of living across India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Passport Fees Jump Up to 75% From July 1. Here’s What Changes for NRIs.
nri-world.excerpt: The Ministry of External Affairs has revised passport charges across the board — fresh applications, renewals, Tatkaal, and replacements all cost more. With 32 million overseas Indians, the timing is hard to ignore.
nri-world.image_caption: An Indian passport. Fee revisions notified by the Ministry of External Affairs take effect on July 1, 2026.
nri-world.nri_angle: India's 32 million overseas Indians rely on passport services for travel, residency, and legal identity. The fee hike affects Gulf renewals, family applications, and consular services worldwide. Paired with broader July 1 financial changes including ITR deadline shifts and credit card reporting rules.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Belfast Burned. An Indian Woman Fed the Families Left Behind.
nri-world.excerpt: Anti-immigration riots in Northern Ireland displaced dozens of minority families. For the Indian community in the UK, the violence has deepened a quiet unease about safety that no advisory can fully address.
nri-world.image_caption: Belfast City Hall, Donegall Square — the heart of a city shaken by anti-immigration violence in June 2026. (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: The Belfast riots forced Indians and other ethnic minorities in Northern Ireland to confront their vulnerability. Ruchira Rangaprasad's community meal drive and INSIGHT UK's safety advisory for Hindu communities reflect a diaspora learning to protect itself in an increasingly hostile European landscape.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora's Philanthropy Machine Just Turned 25. It Raised a Record $3.8 Million in One Night.
nri-world.excerpt: The American India Foundation's silver-jubilee gala honoured BNY, Bharat Masrani and Salil Parekh — and marked a turning point for Indian-American giving that has nearly tripled in six years.
nri-world.image_caption: Bharat Masrani, retired CEO of TD Bank Group, was honoured at AIF's 25th-anniversary gala at Cipriani Wall Street
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-American philanthropy has reached an inflection point, with giving tripling to $4–5 billion and the gap between potential and actual donations shrinking to $1 billion. AIF's gala channels that energy into education, health and livelihoods across India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: She Built the Middleware That Moves Indian Brands Across Borders. EY Just Noticed.
nri-world.excerpt: Somdutta Singh becomes the third and youngest Indian woman to win an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year award, after Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw and Falguni Nayar.
nri-world.image_caption: Somdutta Singh, founder and CEO of Assiduus, is just the third Indian woman to win the EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Southeast award (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Singh's cross-border commerce platform is the infrastructure layer NRIs and Indian exporters depend on. Her recognition at a global entrepreneurship award elevates the visibility of Indian women founders in the diaspora business landscape.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian Law Graduate Just Became CFO of America's Biggest Gym Chain. He Also Runs Its Global Expansion.
nri-world.excerpt: Planet Fitness appoints Sudhanshu Priyadarshi — a National Law School alumnus who has steered finances at Keurig, PepsiCo, and Walmart — as CFO and President, International.
nri-world.image_caption: A Planet Fitness location in Ypsilanti Township, Michigan — part of the chain's 2,700-strong network that Priyadarshi now helps steer
nri-world.nri_angle: Priyadarshi's appointment at Planet Fitness extends the growing pattern of Indian-origin executives reaching the C-suite of major American consumer brands, normalising a career trajectory that was rare a generation ago.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The App the Diaspora Lives On Just Got an Indian Boss
nri-world.excerpt: Kunal Shah, who built CRED from a million dollars of personal capital into a $4.5 billion fintech, will lead WhatsApp globally — the clearest sign yet that Meta's future runs through India.
nri-world.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and the new global head of WhatsApp
nri-world.nri_angle: WhatsApp is the communication backbone of virtually every diaspora family — the morning prayers forwarded from Ahmedabad, the group chat that settles who is cooking for the potluck, the voice notes that keep grandparents present across oceans. An Indian founder now runs it.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Tall Ship Has Sailed 13,000 Miles to Help America Celebrate Its Birthday. The Diaspora Turned Out to Watch.
nri-world.excerpt: INS Sudarshini's five-month voyage from Kochi to Baltimore — with stops in Oman, Egypt, France, and the Canary Islands — culminates in community outreach events that have drawn Indian Americans across the mid-Atlantic.
nri-world.image_caption: INS Sudarshini under sail during a previous transoceanic voyage
nri-world.nri_angle: The ship's community outreach events in Norfolk and Baltimore draw Indian Americans from across the mid-Atlantic corridor — one of the largest concentrations of the diaspora in the US — offering a rare moment of visible Indian presence in a quintessentially American celebration.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Supreme Court Is About to Rule on Whether Babies Born to H-1B Parents Are American Citizens
nri-world.excerpt: A decision expected as early as Monday could strip birthright citizenship from hundreds of thousands of children born each year to parents on temporary visas — including the quarter-million Indians on H-1B status.
nri-world.image_caption: The US Supreme Court building in Washington, where a ruling on birthright citizenship is expected this week
nri-world.nri_angle: This ruling directly affects the quarter-million Indians currently on H-1B visas in America and their families — if upheld, babies born to H-1B holders in the US would not be American citizens, potentially leaving them stateless.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The July 31 Deadline Is Coming. Here's What Every NRI Filing an Indian Tax Return Needs to Know.
nri-world.excerpt: Schedule FA, the DTAA paper trail, the FBAR double bind — a practical guide to the traps that catch diaspora taxpayers every year.
nri-world.image_caption: Tax documents and currency on a desk during filing season
nri-world.nri_angle: Every NRI with Indian income faces the July 31 ITR deadline. The compliance burden is uniquely diaspora-shaped — juggling two tax systems, two sets of forms, and penalties that can reach ₹10 lakh per missed disclosure.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifty Years Ago, a Handful of Hare Krishnas Pulled a Chariot Down Fifth Avenue. Now 25,000 Show Up.
nri-world.excerpt: ISKCON's Ratha Yatra in Manhattan just marked its golden anniversary — a milestone in how the Indian diaspora practises faith in public.
nri-world.image_caption: Devotees pull a decorated Ratha Yatra chariot at an ISKCON festival in the United States
nri-world.nri_angle: The Ratha Yatra is the diaspora's most visible public expression of Hindu devotion in the West. For Indian-American families, ISKCON centres have become anchors of cultural continuity — the neighbourhood temple transplanted to Brooklyn and Trafalgar Square.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Modi Wrote in Creole to a Diaspora That Has Been in Seychelles Since Before America Was a Country
nri-world.excerpt: India's prime minister is visiting a 115-island archipelago in the Indian Ocean where Tamil settlers arrived in 1770 — and where Indians now make up nearly a tenth of the population.
nri-world.image_caption: The clock tower in Victoria, Mahé — the capital of Seychelles and the smallest capital city in the world
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian community in Seychelles is one of the oldest continuous diaspora settlements in the world, yet remains almost invisible to the broader NRI conversation. Modi's visit — and his choice to address them in the local Creole language — underscores how far-flung India's people-to-people ties really are, even in a nation of just 121,000.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Saudi Arabia Just Told 2.4 Million Indians They Can Stop Renting. Few Know What That Actually Means.
nri-world.excerpt: A new digital portal lets foreigners buy property across the Kingdom for the first time — opening the door for millions of Indian workers who have spent decades as tenants in the Gulf's biggest economy.
nri-world.image_caption: The Riyadh skyline — Saudi Arabia's capital and the centre of its expanding real estate market
nri-world.nri_angle: For the 2.4 million Indians living in Saudi Arabia — the largest expatriate group in the Kingdom — the ability to own property transforms the economic equation of Gulf migration from temporary labor to potential long-term investment and stability.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank's CEO Just Said He Won't Stay — and the Stock Dropped 3.3% as a Succession Battle Begins
markets-finance.excerpt: Ashok Vaswani, who took over from founder Uday Kotak just three years ago, informed the board he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in December 2026 — leaving India's fourth-largest private bank searching for its third CEO in four years.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Kotak Mahindra Bank branch, one of the most widely held Indian banking stocks among NRI investors
markets-finance.nri_angle: Kotak Mahindra Bank is one of the most widely held Indian stocks among NRI investors — the CEO transition and valuation correction raise key portfolio questions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The US FDA Just Sent an SOS to Indian Drugmakers for a Cancer Drug It Can't Source Anywhere Else
markets-finance.excerpt: A global ifosfamide shortage has forced America's drug regulator to reach out to Indian manufacturers directly — and the pharma stocks that could benefit are already rallying
markets-finance.image_caption: Pharmaceutical capsules being manufactured — India supplies over 40 percent of America's generic drugs
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian pharma's role as the world's indispensable generic drug supplier creates a structural investment thesis for NRIs, with companies like Cipla and Zydus positioned to capture emergency FDA supply contracts
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Central Bank Is Offering NRIs a Rare Deal — Dollar Deposits at Up to 7.5% With Zero Currency Risk
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI has removed interest rate ceilings on FCNR deposits and is absorbing the full hedging cost. Banks have responded with rate hikes of up to 450 basis points. The window closes September 30.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: This is a direct, time-limited opportunity for NRIs to earn 6-7.5% on dollar deposits in India with no currency risk — a rare combination that may not repeat for years.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Persistent Systems Just Made India's Biggest Mid-Cap IT Bet — a €1 Billion Bid for Germany's Nagarro That Crashed Its Own Stock 11%
markets-finance.excerpt: The Pune-based IT firm's audacious offer for the Munich-headquartered digital engineering company would create a 46,000-person AI services giant, but analysts are questioning the valuation, flagging margin dilution, and watching for a BaFin insider-trading probe.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — Persistent Systems shares fell 11.2% on the BSE following the Nagarro acquisition announcement
markets-finance.nri_angle: The deal reshapes the mid-tier Indian IT landscape that employs tens of thousands of NRIs, creates a company with 37,000 India-based employees, and matters to NRI investors who hold Persistent Systems stock directly or through India-focused mutual funds.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Defence Stocks Have Crushed the Market in 2026 — and the Order Books Suggest They're Just Getting Started
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty India Defence index has surged 25% this year while the Nifty 50 has fallen 8%. HAL, BEL, Data Patterns and Bharat Dynamics are riding record order books, a ₹6.81 lakh crore defence budget, and a government that is dead serious about making India a defence exporter.
markets-finance.image_caption: Two HAL Tejas light combat aircraft flying in formation — the indigenous fighter has become a symbol of India's defence manufacturing ambitions
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's defence sector offers NRI investors a domestic-demand-driven growth story insulated from rupee weakness, with the Nifty Defence index up 25% in 2026 — accessible through NRI portfolio accounts, ETFs and LRS routes.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Retail Investors Just Absorbed the Biggest Foreign Selloff in History — and JP Morgan Says They Won't Stop
markets-finance.excerpt: Foreign portfolio investors have pulled over ₹2.67 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026 — but monthly SIP inflows above ₹30,000 crore have made the market almost self-sustaining.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, the financial heart of India
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors weighing India allocations need to understand that the market is no longer FPI-dependent — SIP-driven domestic flows now set the floor, and tax policy changes make equities India's most efficient savings vehicle.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years Is Threatening to Derail the Post-Oil Rally — and a Super El Niño Could Make It Worse
markets-finance.excerpt: Rainfall is running 43% below average, sugar prices are surging, and Citigroup warns El Niño could cost the global economy up to $7 trillion. India has drawn up contingency plans for over 300 districts — but investors are asking whether the damage is already priced in.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Indian monsoon, the weakest in 11 years, threatens to derail crop yields and the post-oil market rally (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRI investors with exposure to Indian equities, FMCG, and agri-linked sectors, the monsoon deficit is the single biggest near-term variable — and El Niño could turn a manageable shortfall into a prolonged rural demand crisis.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India and the US Are 'Very, Very Close' to a Historic Trade Deal — but One Number Stands in the Way
markets-finance.excerpt: With USTR Jamieson Greer wrapping up talks in New Delhi and Trade Minister Goyal claiming the deal is nearly done, the only remaining obstacle is a politically explosive tariff gap with Pakistan that no Indian leader can accept.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who is leading trade negotiations with the United States
markets-finance.nri_angle: A trade deal would affect Indian stock markets, NRI dollar deposits, remittance exchange rates, and diaspora-heavy sectors like IT, pharma, and AI — plus it determines whether 4.4 million Indian-Americans see deeper economic integration between their two countries.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is About to Launch the Biggest IPO Wave in Its History — and NRI Investors Are Watching Closely
markets-finance.excerpt: Jio Platforms, the National Stock Exchange, Zepto, and SBI Mutual Fund are among at least ₹90,000 crore worth of public offerings lined up for the second half of 2026, led by what could be India's largest-ever listing
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, the heart of India's capital markets
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors can participate in India's historic IPO wave through NRE/NRO demat accounts; the ₹35,000 crore Jio listing alone could be the largest opportunity in Indian market history.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Tata Motors Is Ramping EV Production by 50% — and Turning to China's Chery to Build Its Premium Electric Future
markets-finance.excerpt: With EV bookings surging 2.5 times on rising fuel costs, Tata is scaling output from 10,000 to 15,000 units a month while licensing Chery's Freelander platform for its delayed Avinya luxury EVs — a strategy that blends domestic manufacturing ambition with quiet Chinese technology dependence.
markets-finance.image_caption: A Tata Nexon EV, the best-selling electric car in India, on display
markets-finance.nri_angle: Tata Motors stock is a bellwether for NRI investors in India's manufacturing story — the EV pivot and Chinese tech dependency create both opportunity and risk for diaspora portfolios.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Doubled Gold Tariffs to Save the Rupee — Now Smugglers Are Filling the Gap
markets-finance.excerpt: A tariff hike from 6% to 15% was meant to staunch an $84 billion gold import bill. Instead, grey-market inflows could hit 100 tons this year, jewellers are pivoting to lighter designs, and NRIs heading home for weddings face painfully higher costs.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold jewellery on display at an Indian jewellery store during the wedding season
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs travelling home for weddings face gold jewellery costs up 10% overnight, and the grey-market discount raises questions about whether to buy at home or abroad — while sovereign gold bonds remain an NRI-friendly alternative.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: South Korea's KOSPI Crashed Twice in a Week — India's Markets Logged a Third Straight Weekly Gain
markets-finance.excerpt: While circuit breakers halted trading in Seoul as Samsung and SK Hynix plummeted over 10 percent in an AI-fuelled rout, India's Nifty and Sensex quietly extended their winning streak, insulated by falling oil prices, RBI measures and a market structure that doesn't bet the house on one sector.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai — home to a market that dodged the global AI selloff this week
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to both Indian and global markets saw a stark lesson this week: India's diversified index structure and domestic macro tailwinds offered shelter from a tech-driven storm that hammered concentrated bets elsewhere.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Millennials and Gen Z Are Aging Faster Inside Their Bodies — and It May Be Fueling a Cancer Surge
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark study of 164,000 people across the US and UK found that younger generations show significantly more biological 'wear and tear' than their parents did at the same age — and the gap is linked to rising early-onset cancers in the gut, lungs, and uterus.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A researcher examines blood biomarker data in a laboratory setting
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated metabolic and inflammatory risk factors that accelerate biological aging — this study adds urgency to earlier screening and lifestyle intervention for young NRI professionals.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Exercise Alone Can Tackle Six of the 14 Risk Factors for Dementia — and May Prevent Half of All Cases
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A University of Minnesota study identifies 14 modifiable lifestyle factors behind cognitive decline, and finds that consistent physical exercise addresses six of them at once — from blood pressure to depression — offering the single most powerful intervention against dementia.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult exercises outdoors, an activity linked to significant dementia prevention benefits
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Dementia in India is projected to nearly triple by 2050, and South Asians carry elevated metabolic risk — exercise is the single most accessible intervention for NRI families and aging parents.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Brain Starts Calming Down in Just Two Minutes of Meditation — and Peak Zen Arrives at Seven
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Harvard and NIMHANS brain-scan study mapped exactly when meditation rewires your neural activity — and even complete beginners showed the same timing as seasoned practitioners
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person meditating — researchers found the brain begins calming within two to three minutes
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NIMHANS-Harvard collaboration bridges Indian contemplative traditions with Western neuroscience, offering busy NRI professionals a research-backed seven-minute prescription for stress relief
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Nearly Half of Adults Over 65 Actually Got Sharper With Age — and Their Mindset Was the Key
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Yale study tracking 11,000 Americans for 12 years found that positive beliefs about aging predicted real improvements in cognition and physical function — not just slower decline
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An elderly couple walking together in a park — the Yale study measured physical improvement through walking speed
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs watching parents age from afar can take heart: positive attitudes about aging are not just cultural values but measurable health interventions, and the conversations families have across continents may shape real outcomes
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Hormone Therapy Slashes Osteoporosis Risk by 69% — and South Asian Women May Have the Most to Gain
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study presented at ENDO 2026 adds to growing evidence that menopausal hormone therapy protects bone density. For South Asian women — who face earlier menopause and higher fracture risk — the findings carry extra urgency.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A bone density scanner used to check for osteoporosis. (Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 2.0)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian women experience menopause earlier on average and have higher baseline bone resorption rates, making HRT's bone-protective benefits especially relevant for NRI women and their mothers back home.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Remote Work Is Making People Lonelier — and the Effects Are Worst for Those Living Alone
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark study of 588,000 workers published in Science found that remote work accounts for roughly a third of the post-pandemic rise in mental distress. For NRI tech workers far from family, the findings hit close to home.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A person working alone from home on a laptop
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRI tech workers — many of them remote, many living alone thousands of miles from family — face a compounded version of the isolation this study describes, with immigration-related social barriers layered on top.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: GLP-1 Poison Control Calls Have Surged Fivefold — and a New Pill That Doesn't Require Fasting Could Change Everything
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Journal of Medical Toxicology study reveals over 10,000 GLP-1 exposures reported to U.S. poison centers, while a new oral drug published in Nature Medicine shows 16% weight loss with no empty-stomach requirement — developments that matter deeply for the South Asian diaspora.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic (semaglutide) injection pen, the GLP-1 drug that now accounts for 64% of all poison control calls in this drug class
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest global rates of type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome, making them one of the fastest-growing demographics on GLP-1 drugs in the US — and disproportionately affected by both the safety risks and the promise of cheaper oral alternatives.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A New Blood Test Catches 90% of Aggressive Prostate Cancers That the Standard PSA Misses — and Only 6% of Men Are Even Being Screened
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The Stockholm3 test, validated in a 12,000-man trial published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, detected aggressive prostate cancer far more reliably than the decades-old PSA — a breakthrough that matters for South Asian men who face cultural barriers to screening.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Blood test tubes in a medical laboratory — the Stockholm3 test uses a single blood draw to detect aggressive prostate cancer
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian men in the US often delay or avoid prostate screening due to cultural stigma around the exam, and prostate cancer is the second most common cancer in men globally — this blood test could remove one of the biggest barriers to early detection.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Type of Fat in Your Kitchen May Matter More Than How Much You Use — and a New Review Shows Why
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Palmitic acid, the dominant saturated fat in ghee, palm oil and processed snacks, drives insulin resistance at the molecular level. Oleic acid — abundant in olive oil and mustard oil — may reverse it. A University of Barcelona review in Trends in Endocrinology & Metabolism lays out the evidence.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A bottle of extra-virgin olive oil, rich in oleic acid, which a new review links to lower insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes protection
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have the highest insulin resistance rates in the world, and the palmitic-acid-heavy fats in traditional Indian cooking — ghee, palm oil, vanaspati — are now directly implicated at the molecular level.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Gut Bacteria May Explain Why Coffee Wrecks Your Sleep — and a 7,000-Person Study Just Mapped the Connection
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Nature Communications study of nearly 7,000 Dutch adults found 137 bacterial species linked to sleep quality. Two Clostridia species appear to mediate coffee's effect on social jet lag — the gap between your weekday and weekend sleep clocks.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A freshly brewed cup of coffee — a new study finds gut bacteria may mediate its disruptive effect on sleep timing
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are heavy coffee and chai consumers, and NRI tech workers face extreme social jet lag from cross-timezone schedules — gut microbiome differences could amplify or mitigate these effects.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Leafy Greens in Your Thali May Be Quietly Protecting Your Lungs — and a Major New Study Shows How
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers tracked 179,000 adults for over a decade and found that those who ate the most vitamin K1 — abundant in spinach, kale, and methi — had a 16% lower risk of chronic lung disease.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fresh leafy greens including spinach, kale, and other vitamin K1-rich vegetables
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian cuisine's rich tradition of leafy greens — palak, methi, sarson, bathua — provides among the highest vitamin K1 intakes of any food culture, offering NRIs a familiar dietary tool to protect lung health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One in Four Depression Cases May Be Driven by Inflammation — and Standard Antidepressants Often Don't Work for Them
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Growing evidence points to a distinct subtype of depression fuelled by chronic inflammation, with implications for South Asians who carry higher metabolic and inflammatory risk.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Emerging research links chronic inflammation to a distinct subtype of depression that resists standard antidepressant treatment
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry elevated baseline inflammation from metabolic syndrome at higher rates than any other ethnic group, meaning NRIs may be disproportionately affected by inflammation-driven depression — and less likely to respond to standard SSRIs.

food.title: The $5 Alphonso: Inside the Mango Vans Rolling Through America's Indian Neighbourhoods
food.excerpt: India's mango exports to the US have already surpassed last year's full-season total, driven by WhatsApp-coordinated delivery vans, surging diaspora demand, and a season extended by northern Indian varieties.
food.image_caption: Fresh Indian Alphonso mangoes, the most sought-after variety among diaspora communities in the US
food.nri_angle: Indian mangoes are a visceral link to home for NRIs — the WhatsApp-driven delivery networks and record exports reflect a diaspora willing to pay a premium for a taste of identity.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From 7-Eleven to James Beard: The Improbable Rise of Chef Suresh Sundas
food.excerpt: The Nepali-born chef who taught himself to cook in his mother's kitchen has become the first person from Nepal to be named a James Beard Award finalist — and he's rewriting the rules of Indian food in Washington, DC.
food.image_caption: Daru restaurant in Washington DC's H Street corridor, co-founded by Chef Suresh Sundas and Dante Datta
food.nri_angle: Sundas's journey from Nepali immigrant working at 7-Eleven to history-making James Beard finalist embodies the unsung South Asian culinary talent reshaping American dining.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Beyond the Buffet: Indian Food Finally Gets Its Fast-Casual Moment in America
food.excerpt: From Curry Up Now's tikka burritos to Tarka Indian Kitchen's Texas expansion, Indian cuisine is carving out a fast-casual niche that the industry has predicted for years — and this time, the numbers suggest it's real.
food.image_caption: An Indian food platter featuring grilled chicken, naan, fresh sauces, and salad — the kind of accessible presentation driving the fast-casual boom
food.nri_angle: The fast-casual boom means Indian food — the chaat, kathi rolls, dosas — is finally being presented to mainstream America the way diaspora communities have always known it deserves.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Vikas Khanna's Unstoppable Year: From TIME 100 to Harvard's Stage to a Chai Empire
food.excerpt: The Amritsar-born chef's 2026 has been a masterclass in turning cultural pride into global influence — and he is just getting started.
food.image_caption: Chef Vikas Khanna, the Amritsar-born Michelin-starred restaurateur and TIME 100 honoree
food.nri_angle: Khanna's trajectory — from Amritsar to the TIME 100 — embodies the diaspora's aspiration that Indian excellence can be celebrated on the world's biggest stages.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Chai Wars Come to New York: How Two Bengali Brothers and a Comedian Are Taking On Starbucks
food.excerpt: Kolkata Chai Co. just landed a Michelin-starred backer in Vikas Khanna, adding to Hasan Minhaj's earlier investment — and the $10 billion masala chai market is paying attention.
food.image_caption: A glass of masala chai brewed the traditional way with spices, milk and strong black tea
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who have long winced at the 'chai tea latte,' the rise of authentic chai brands feels like a small but meaningful cultural correction — and an entrepreneurial success story rooted in the immigrant experience.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Curry Ketchup and Tandoori Naanwiches: India Storms America's Biggest Food Trade Show
food.excerpt: At this weekend's Summer Fancy Food Show in New York, Indian flavors were everywhere — and the industry's trend-spotters are calling it a mainstream moment.
food.image_caption: Colorful Indian spices displayed at a market — flavors now finding mainstream shelf space across America
food.nri_angle: The mainstreaming of Indian flavors at America's biggest food trade show is both a point of pride and a test of authenticity for NRIs who have long wanted their cuisine taken seriously.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Gymkhana's Kitchen Goes Retail: Michelin-Starred Indian Sauces Land at Whole Foods
food.excerpt: The London restaurant group behind eight Michelin stars raises $8.5 million to bring its simmer sauces to American home kitchens, marking what insiders call Indian food's 'premium moment.'
food.image_caption: Gymkhana's Michelin-starred Indian cooking sauces are now available at Whole Foods locations across the United States (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Indian Americans have watched their cuisine be relegated to the ethnic aisle; Gymkhana's Whole Foods launch signals a premium repositioning that the diaspora has long advocated for.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: The Chatpata Comeback: India Rediscovers Its Bold, Unapologetic Flavors
food.excerpt: The Godrej Food Trends Report 2026 declares bold, piquant tastes the defining palate of the year, as India's food culture moves from Instagram minimalism to storytelling and 'flavor collisions.'
food.image_caption: A plate of papri chaat garnished with yoghurt, chutney, and fresh coriander
food.nri_angle: The chatpata flavor comeback and food storytelling revolution validate what NRIs have always known — that Indian food's depth deserves more than the 'mild-medium-spicy' treatment it gets abroad.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Udupi to the Pacific Northwest: Hari Nayak Plots Indian Cuisine's Next Frontier
food.excerpt: The Michelin-recognised chef is opening a new restaurant at Woodinville's Harvest Yard that filters India's culinary traditions through the bounty of the Pacific Northwest.
food.image_caption: A masala dosa, the classic South Indian dish from the Udupi tradition that shaped chef Hari Nayak's culinary philosophy (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: A Michelin-star Indian chef opening in the Pacific Northwest gives the large Seattle-area Indian American community a fine-dining destination that redefines Indian cuisine beyond neighbourhood curry houses.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Butter Chicken at Costco: How Indian Food Brands Are Storming America's Grocery Aisles
food.excerpt: From Quicklly's launch at 2,500 ALDI stores to Truly Indian's NEXTY Award nods, packaged Indian cuisine is muscling into mainstream American retail at an unprecedented pace.
food.image_caption: Butter chicken served with butter naan, the iconic dish now available across American grocery chains from Costco to Trader Joe's (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Butter chicken and tikka masala naan at Costco and ALDI represent a cultural milestone for Indian Americans who have long wished for their staple foods in mainstream American grocery stores.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: Copper and Courage: How a Punjabi Family Rebuilt Their Las Vegas Restaurant and Earned a James Beard Nod
food.excerpt: When the Dhillon family's beloved Indian restaurant was demolished with the Hawaiian Marketplace, their son brought it back — and in its first year, Tamba became a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist.
food.image_caption: An Indian dinner spread at a restaurant, featuring curry, rice, and traditional accompaniments
food.nri_angle: The Dhillon family's journey from Punjabi immigrants running a small Monterey restaurant in 1989 to James Beard Best New Restaurant finalists in Las Vegas mirrors the broader Indian American story of ambition and cultural pride.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

food.title: From Chicago's Michelin Star to Phoenix and Hudson Yards: The Sujan Sarkar Playbook
food.excerpt: The Kolkata-born chef behind Indienne is building a multi-city, multi-concept Indian restaurant empire — and mentoring the next generation of desi chefs along the way.
food.image_caption: The Michelin Guide — Chef Sujan Sarkar's Indienne in Chicago holds a coveted Michelin star (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: Indian American chef Sujan Sarkar is building what may become the first Michelin-scale Indian restaurant empire in the US, proving that desi cuisine belongs at every level of American dining.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: Gulf Ceasefire Unravels as Iran Fires Missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain. India’s Seafarers Pay the Price.
carousel.excerpt: Three Indian sailors are dead, 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, and the fragile US-Iran deal is falling apart — leaving New Delhi caught between its closest strategic partner and its citizens’ safety.
carousel.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman that has become the epicenter of the US-Iran conflict.
carousel.image_credit: NASA/MODIS, Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
carousel.nri_angle: India's 9 million Gulf workers face direct risk from the escalation. Three Indian seafarers died on the MT Settebello, prompting India to summon the US envoy. Thousands more remain stranded on ships in the Gulf. India's oil imports and domestic inflation are directly tied to Hormuz stability.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: South Korea Just Bet $576 Billion on Chips. India Has Bet $10 Billion. That Ratio Tells a Story.

carousel.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian Americans work at semiconductor firms like Intel, Qualcomm and Micron — Korea's massive bet reshapes the global chip talent map and raises questions about India's ability to compete.

carousel.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank's CEO Just Said He Won't Stay — and the Stock Dropped 3.3% as a Succession Battle Begins
carousel.excerpt: Ashok Vaswani, who took over from founder Uday Kotak just three years ago, informed the board he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in December 2026 — leaving India's fourth-largest private bank searching for its third CEO in four years.
carousel.image_caption: A Kotak Mahindra Bank branch, one of the most widely held Indian banking stocks among NRI investors
carousel.nri_angle: Kotak Mahindra Bank is one of the most widely held Indian stocks among NRI investors — the CEO transition and valuation correction raise key portfolio questions.
